title: Number of Intersections
explanation: LESSON OBJECTIVE
Count distinct real intersections of function graphs by solving f(x)=g(x), including parameter cases.
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
Each shared ordered pair (x,y) satisfies both equations. For functions, each distinct real x solving f(x)=g(x) produces exactly one shared point.
KEY DEFINITIONS
An intersection is a shared point. A repeated root counts once. The discriminant of Ax²+Bx+C=0 is D=B²−4AC. Coincident graphs have infinitely many shared points.
CORE RULE
For A≠0: D>0 gives two real intersections, D=0 one, D<0 none. For A=0,B≠0 the equation is linear and gives one; A=B=0,C≠0 gives none; A=B=C=0 gives infinitely many.
HOW IT WORKS
Set f(x)=g(x), collect terms, check whether the resulting equation is quadratic, linear, contradictory or an identity. Use D only for a genuine quadratic; substitute x back to find y.
WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — TWO
y=x² and y=4 imply x²=4, x=−2 or 2. Shared points: (−2,4) and (2,4).
WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — ONE
y=x² and y=4x−4 imply (x−2)²=0. One shared point: (2,4).
WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — ZERO
y=x²+5 and y=1 imply x²+4=0, impossible over real numbers.
WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — LINEAR CANCELLATION
y=x²+3x+2 and y=x²−2x+7 imply 5x=5, x=1 and y=6. One intersection despite the original quadratics.
WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — PARAMETER
y=x²+k and y=4x−1 imply x²−4x+k+1=0. D=12−4k; exactly one intersection requires k=3. The shared point is (2,7), since 4(2)−1=7 and 2²+3=7.
GRAPH / VISUAL
The deterministic graph of y=x²−4x+1 and y=x−3 has shared points (1,−2) and (4,1). Algebra: x²−5x+4=(x−1)(x−4)=0.
DESMOS STRATEGY

Enter y=x²−4x+1 and y=x−3. Look for (1,−2) and (4,1). Use it to answer by counting shared points. Why it works: each ordered pair satisfies both equations. Faster or not? Graphing checks a picture quickly; exact algebra is faster for parameter questions.
COMMON MISTAKES
Do not count a repeated root twice, count complex roots as visible intersections, or apply the discriminant after squared terms cancel. Identical equations have infinitely many intersections.
EXAM STRATEGY
If the question asks only how many, stop after identifying the number of distinct real solutions. For parameter questions, set D=0 for one or D>0 for two, provided the equation is quadratic.
QUICK CHECK
Try: (a) y=x² and y=9; (b) y=x²+3 and y=3; (c) y=x²+4 and y=0; (d) y=x²+2x+1 and y=x²−2x+1. Answers: 2, 1, 0, 1.
LESSON RECAP
Equate, simplify, classify. Quadratic D>0: two; D=0: one; D<0: zero. Linear: one; contradiction: zero; identity: infinitely many.
NEXT STEP
Complete 18 Practice Problems, review the 18 aligned Answers & Solutions, then submit the five-question Test. English and Arabic full lesson videos reinforce the same skill.
practice: How many intersections do y=x² and y=4 have?
x²=4 gives x=±2, two distinct real x-values.
How many intersections do y=x²+2 and y=2 have?
x²=0 gives x=0, one distinct real x-value.
How many intersections do y=x²+5 and y=1 have?
How many intersections do y=x²−3x and y=x+5 have?
How many intersections do y=x²+2x+3 and y=2x+3 have?
Subtract the equations: x²=0, so x=0 only.
How many intersections do y=2x²+5 and y=x²+1 have?
How many intersections do y=x²+3 and y=x²−2x+1 have?
How many intersections do y=3x²−4x+2 and y=x²+2x−3 have?
How many intersections do y=x²−6x+9 and y=0 have?
How many intersections do y=−x²+6x−4 and y=2x have?
How many intersections do y=x²−1 and y=−x²+7 have?
For y=x²+k and y=4x−1, find k for exactly one intersection.
x²−4x+(k+1)=0 has D=12−4k; set D=0, k=3.
How many intersections do y=x²+2x+5 and y=2x+1 have?
For y=x²+bx+9 and y=0, find all b for exactly one intersection.
Find the exact intersection point of y=x²+3x+2 and y=x²−2x+7.
For y=x²+2 and y=2x+k, which k values give exactly two intersections?
x²−2x+2−k=0 has D=4(k−1)>0 precisely when k>1.
For y=x²+k and y=−x²+4x+1, find k for exactly one intersection.
2x²−4x+k−1=0 has D=24−8k; set to zero, k=3.
For y=x²+ax+4 and y=2x, find all a for exactly one intersection.
